words.meaning: decided or controlled by technical experts rather than by politicians or ordinary people
words.example: The technocratic committee imposed the new data policy without consulting the public.
words.persian: مبنی بر حکومت متخصصان فنی؛ تصمیم‌گیری توسط کارشناسان فنی

words.meaning: the science of communication and automatic control in machines and living things
words.example: Modern cybernetics treats the brain and the computer as variations on the same information-processing system.
words.persian: علم کنترل و ارتباط در ماشین‌ها و موجودات زنده

words.meaning: strong public anger and backlash against powerful technology companies
words.example: The techlash of the last decade forced governments to confront the power of the platform giants.
words.persian: واکنش منفی و خشم گستردهٔ عمومی علیه شرکت‌های بزرگ فناوری

words.meaning: opposition to new technology, named after the nineteenth-century workers who destroyed new machines
words.example: His refusal to own a smartphone is less luddism than a deliberate choice to protect his attention.

words.meaning: the belief that every social or political problem has a technological solution
words.example: Technosolutionism tempts politicians to fund apps instead of fixing the underlying problem.
words.persian: باور به اینکه هر مشکلی راه‌حل فناورانه دارد

words.meaning: a deceptive design trick in an app or website that manipulates users
words.example: The checkout page used a classic dark pattern, hiding the cancel button in pale grey text.
words.persian: ترفند فریبندهٔ طراحی برای دستکاری کاربر

words.meaning: the idea that technological and economic change should be accelerated rather than slowed down
words.example: Silicon Valley accelerationism treats every regulation as an obstacle to inevitable progress.
words.persian: باور به شتاب دادن به تغییرات فناورانه و اقتصادی

grammar.title: Fronting and Word Order for Emphasis
grammar.explanation:
**Fronting** means moving part of a sentence to the **beginning** for emphasis or dramatic effect. Instead of "A castle stood on the hill," a novelist writes "**On the hill stood** a castle," and the image lands much harder.

After a fronted place or direction, a short verb like **be**, **stand**, **lie**, **come**, or **go** can come **before a noun subject**: "**Into the room walked** a technocratic committee." With a pronoun subject, keep normal order: "Here **it comes**," never "Here comes it."

Adjectives, participles, **so**, and **such** can also be fronted, with inversion of the verb and subject: "**Gone are** the days of unchecked accelerationism." "**So strong was** the techlash **that** the giants changed course." "**Such was** his fury **that** he could not speak."

You can also front an **object** for contrast, with no inversion at all: "**This dark pattern** I cannot accept." The rest of the sentence keeps its normal order, which makes the fronted word strike even harder.
examples: *On the top of the hill **stood** an old castle.* (place + verb + subject)
*Into the room **walked** a man in a black coat.* (direction + verb + subject)
***Gone are** the days of cheap flights.* (participle fronting)
***So difficult was** the exam **that** only two students passed.* (so... that)
***Lucky are** those who love their jobs.* (adjective fronting)
***Some things** you just can't explain.* (object fronting, no inversion)

practice.q: Rewrite with fronting: A technocratic committee sat around the long glass table.
practice.a: Around the long glass table sat a technocratic committee.

practice.q: Rewrite with so-fronting: The techlash was so strong that the companies changed their policies.
practice.a: So strong was the techlash that the companies changed their policies.

practice.q: Rewrite by fronting the object: I cannot accept this dark pattern.
practice.a: This dark pattern I cannot accept.

practice.q: Rewrite with fronting: Mr. Hale practiced his gentle luddism on the quiet farm.
practice.a: On the quiet farm Mr. Hale practiced his gentle luddism.
